items.title: A Deep Learning and Digital Twin Framework for Automated Crack Detection and Maintenance-Oriented Condition Assessment of Industrial Buildings
items.abstract: The maintenance of industrial buildings is essential to ensure the operability, safety, and efficiency of these facilities, which are key pillars of the industrial sector. Proper maintenance management has a direct impact on productivity and the continuity of operational processes. However, managing the maintenance of these built assets pose significant challenges, particularly in terms of efficiency in inspection, diagnosis, and the planning of corrective and preventive activities, requiring substantial investment to preserve functionality and prevent disruptions. To address these challenges, this paper presents the development of an intelligent system for advanced damage diagnosis in industrial buildings. The system integrates the MIVES multi-criteria decision-making methodology to objectively assess the structural condition of built assets, incorporating complementary technologies: drones for inspection; artificial intelligence (AI) for data analysis and automatic damage detection; extended reality (XR) for the relocalisation of previously captured environments and the spatial positioning of identified damage; and radiance fields (such as 3D Gaussian Splatting) for 3D scene reconstruction and digital twin generation. A prototype workflow for damage detection was developed by training deep-learning algorithms trained on field images of pathologies in industrial built assets and generating digital twins of the facility using photogrammetry techniques and 3D Gaussian Splatting. This workflow supports the detection and visualization of potential pathologies and provides the data necessary for their objective assessment within the MIVES-base condition condition-assessment framework. These developments are integrated into an application that allows managers and asset owners to access and track inspection information through structured damage records, spatial localization, and digital visualization tools that support maintenance planning and decision-making.

items.title: A Framework for Identifying and Understanding Cognitive Biases in Artificial Intelligence–Assisted Radiology
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) creates new susceptibility to diagnostic error in radiology related to the cognitive processes by which radiologists' interpretations incorporate AI outputs. This Perspective presents a conceptual framework for cognitive biases in AI-assisted radiology linking specific biases to radiologist-AI interactions. The framework uses dual-process theory, recognizing fast intuitive and deliberate analytic modes of information processing, as an organizing model for understanding cognitive processes underlying radiologists' decisions and their potential contribution to bias. Across seven decision scenarios spanning image viewing, findings interpretation, and contextual integration, the framework examines how AI output timing, radiologist-AI agreement, trust calibration, and reader expertise influence decision-making. We identify adaptive heuristics that support efficient decisions but, when misapplied or overrelied upon, increase susceptibility to complacency, confirmation, automation, distrust, anchoring, and usual implication bias, and increase behavioral risk of use without qualification. We highlight AI paradoxes emerging from the framework of despecialization, system fragility, and deskilling. Finally, we propose strategies targeting these cognitive biases, including education and experiential learning, workflow and interface design, clinical oversight, and performance monitoring. This framework provides a structured basis for generating testable hypotheses and designing AI-assisted radiology systems that preserve the strengths of human expertise and AI while supporting calibrated reliance.

items.title: A generalizable 3D dose prediction across heterogeneous cohorts: A framework developed for the 2025 AAPM GDP‐HMM challenge
items.abstract: Abstract Background Manual radiotherapy treatment planning is labor‐intensive, subjective, and highly variable across planners and institutions. Deep learning has emerged as a promising approach for estimating achievable three‐dimensional (3D) dose distributions for a given plan (hereafter: dose prediction) by directly mapping patient anatomy and beam geometry to voxel‐wise dose. However, achieving robust generalization across diverse anatomical sites, prescriptions, and institutions remains a major challenge, particularly under computational constraints required for clinical deployment. Purpose We sought to develop and evaluate a generalizable, computationally efficient 3D dose prediction framework capable of spanning heterogeneous multi‐site and multi‐cohort datasets, as defined in the 2025 AAPM Generalizable Dose Prediction for Heterogeneous Multi‐Cohort and Multi‐Site (GDP‐HMM) Grand Challenge. Our goal was to design a model that not only achieved state‐of‐the‐art voxel‐wise accuracy but also maintained clinically meaningful dose‐volume and geometric characteristics across diverse cases. Methods We implemented a fully convolutional 3D dose‐prediction model adapted from the MedNeXt architecture, which was originally introduced as a high‐capacity convolutional backbone for medical image segmentation and is well suited to volumetric dense prediction tasks. The network accepted multimodal inputs comprising CT, PTV/OAR masks, beam and angle plates, and scalar plan metadata. A composite loss function combined voxel‐wise L 1 , body‐masked weighted L 1 , structure‐wise moment‐matching, and gradient‐based penalties to jointly preserve spatial fidelity and dosimetric accuracy. The model was trained on the fixed GDP‐HMM dataset consisting of 2876 training plans, 356 validation plans, and a held‐out test set of 498 plans using random 3D patches and evaluated by mean absolute error (MAE), homogeneity index (HI), and conformity indices (CI100%, CI50%). Ablation studies quantified the contribution of each loss component to overall performance. Statistical comparisons used paired Wilcoxon tests with false discovery rate correction. Results The proposed model achieved a mean voxel‐wise MAE of 2.04 Gy on the validation set, outperforming the challenge baseline (2.54 Gy). An ensemble with the baseline further improved MAE to 1.94 Gy on the validation set and 2.071 Gy on the held‐out test set, corresponding to the lowest test‐set MAE and first‐place overall ranking in the GDP‐HMM Challenge. Predicted dose distributions preserved key plan characteristics, with ΔHI, ΔCI 100% , and ΔCI 50% narrowly centered around zero, indicating consistent target coverage and dose conformity. Protocol‐specific evaluations for head‐and‐neck and lung cohorts demonstrated close alignment with reference plans, with no systematic degradation in OAR endpoints. Ablation experiments showed that removing gradient‐based terms increased MAE by 0.50 Gy, while excluding the moment‐matching term increased MAE by 0.06 Gy confirming that both gradient‐ and moment‐based constraints enhanced spatial and dosimetric fidelity. Conclusion We present a generalizable 3D dose prediction framework that achieves state‐of‐the‐art accuracy while satisfying stringent runtime requirements (< 3s per case on < 24 GB GPU memory). By integrating gradient‐aware and moment‐based constraints within a MedNeXt backbone, the model preserved clinical DVH endpoints and geometric plan features. These findings demonstrate that carefully engineered loss formulations are pivotal for cross‐institutional generalization. The framework offers a foundation for rapid dose prediction that could accelerate treatment planning, reduce inter‐planner variability, and enable intelligent automation in radiotherapy workflows.

items.title: A Human-Stiffness-Based Simulator for Ergonomic Evaluation of Pistol-Grip Power Tool Reaction
items.abstract: Powered pistol-grip fastening tools can produce substantial handle rotation during torque build-up, which may contribute to operator overuse injuries. This study developed and evaluated a human-stiffness-based physical simulator for a controlled relative comparison of fastening variables affecting peak handle rotation. The simulator used a DC-powered pistol-grip tool, which was constrained to rotate about its spindle axis, with a double-acting pneumatic cylinder providing resistance set according to a specified human-derived stiffness. The evaluation used stiffness data from 10 operators at 5 and 7.5 N·m, with simulator peak displacement compared to in vivo measurements using paired analyses. The simulator was then used as a screening platform to examine the effect of target torque and, at 7.5 N·m, the effects of fastener material, drive style, head type, and spindle speed. The simulator overpredicted human peak displacement, with mean biases of 14.72° at 5 N·m and 10.29° at 7.5 N·m. The peak rotation increased by 15.0% when torque was increased from 5 to 7.5 N·m (p = 0.022). Torx Plus style fasteners produced 11.5% less rotation than Hex drive fasteners; fastener material significantly affected rotation; head type did not; and rotation was substantially lower at 160 rpm. Although the simulator did not reproduce absolute human displacement without bias, the results support its use as a screening platform for relative comparison under fixed mechanical boundary conditions rather than as an absolute predictor of human displacement or injury risk.

items.title: A Landscape Review of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Enabled Teacher Professional Development at Scale
items.abstract: Teacher Professional Development (TPD) significantly influences student learning, yet implementing equitable, quality, and efficient TPD at scale remains a persistent challenge. Emerging technologies—particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI)—offer promising avenues for addressing tensions between localisation and personalisation, but a comprehensive understanding of AI’s role in scaling in-service TPD remains lacking. Guided by the overarching question of how AI enables in-service TPD to be implemented at scale with equity, quality, and efficiency, this landscape review examines three research questions: how AI-enabled TPD programmes address equity, quality, and efficiency at scale; what roles AI plays in enabling TPD at scale; and what promising practices and lessons emerge from such programmes. The review draws conceptually on the World Bank Group’s Technology for Teaching (T4T) framework, which delineates three sequential stages of technology-enhanced TPD: Access, Engage, and Apply. Sources included peer-reviewed studies, policy documents, and grey literature with a pre-defined typology. From an initial pool of 576 articles, 504 were screened after removing duplicates; 34 articles directly addressing the research questions underwent full-text review, supplemented by 59 partially aligned sources. Findings indicate that AI-enabled TPDs address equity, quality, and efficiency at scale by expanding equitable access for teachers of less mainstream K-12 subjects and geographically distant populations while supporting teacher retention by fostering meaningful learning and reducing administrative burden. Regarding roles that AI plays in enabling TPD at scale, AI’s principal affordances include expanding teachers’ knowledge base and learning assets, functioning as a personalised learning coach, and supporting classroom learning management beyond the TPD itself. Common practices that are tentatively effective emerged from the findings include AI chatbots, AI-assisted evaluation reports, and AI-enabled automation, with strong AI-capable leadership emerging as a potentially critical enabler. This review paper also provided practical implications for TPD practitioners, as well as directions for future research. The review’s primary limitations include the scarcity of global research on the topic, the threat of knowledge coloniality, and language constraints that affect the availability and validity of documentation.

items.title: A Large Language Model–Guided Q‐Learning Method for Food Safety Sampling Decision‐Making
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Food safety sampling is a critical measure for safeguarding public health; however, current regulatory practices are challenged by fragmented risk signals, constrained inspection resources, and suboptimal inspection efficiency. To address these issues, this paper proposes a food safety sampling decision‐making method based on large language models (LLM)–guided Q‐learning. First, we leverage LLMs to extract and analyze key elements from unstructured online food safety public opinion data. This is integrated with clustering analysis and the entropy weight method to achieve quantitative risk assessment and grading. Subsequently, a food category–region risk score matrix is constructed, and the allocation of sampling frequency is formalized as a sequential decision‐making problem under resource constraints. Q‐learning is then introduced to learn optimal sampling strategies, using LLM‐generated structured heuristic values as prior guidance, thereby reducing ineffective exploration and enhancing training efficiency. Experimental results, based on data from 30 provincial administrative regions, 457 municipalities/counties, and 25 food categories, generated 4690 risk evaluation records as effective inputs for decision‐making. The results demonstrate that the derived sampling strategies align with risk priors, allocating higher sampling intensity to high‐risk food category–region combinations while maintaining coverage balance across food categories and regions. Compared to the baseline without heuristic guidance, LLM guidance significantly reduces convergence iterations while maintaining steady‐state rewards. This indicates that the proposed method accelerates policy learning without compromising long‐term returns. In conclusion, this study validates that the proposed method achieves a closed‐loop integration of risk assessment and decision optimization, providing a data‐driven methodology for intelligent food safety regulation.

items.title: A model for enhancing the quality of geography education based on the integration of Artificial Intelligence and Geographic Information Systems
items.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) is increasingly central to improving the quality of geography education. This study developed a model intended for enhancing geography education quality based on AI-GIS integration and empirically examined future geography teachers’ readiness to adopt these technologies, drawing on a survey of 100 bachelor's, master's, and doctoral students in geography at al-Farabi Kazakh National University (27 items across three blocks: socio-intellectual characteristics, experience and integration, and professional/ethical issues; Cronbach's α = 0.78, χ 2 (3) = 24.56, p < 0.001). Sixty-seven percent of students reported readiness to use AI-GIS technologies (12% fully ready, 55% ready but requiring further training), and an equal share wished to develop their knowledge in this area further; familiarity was higher for AI (68%) than for GIS (26%) or GeoAI (8%); 99% had used ChatGPT or a similar tool, and ArcGIS was the most common GIS platform (66%). Readiness to use the technologies was associated with GIS familiarity ( ρ = 0.51), GIS proficiency ( ρ = 0.47), and GeoAI knowledge ( ρ = 0.43), but not with general AI familiarity ( ρ = 0.07); H3 and H4 were supported, H1 was not, and H2 was reported as a descriptive result. Although 88% of students viewed AI-GIS integration as beneficial to instructional quality, 67% were unaware of algorithmic bias issues and only 6% had applied these technologies in teaching practice. The results informed a proposed five-component model (content, technological, methodological, integrative, and competency) that has not yet been tested empirically. It is intended for improving teacher-training programs, designing practical courses, and developing future teachers’ digital competence, critical thinking, and ethical awareness.

items.title: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Dynamic Constitutional (Prakriti) Profiling and Personalized Ayurvedic Interventions
items.abstract: Traditional Ayurvedic diagnostics rely on determining an individual's baseline constitution (Prakriti) and acute functional imbalances (Vikriti) through qualitative clinical evaluations and longitudinal lifestyle assessments. While foundational to personalized holistic care, manual constitutional profiling exhibits inter-practitioner variability, requires substantial clinical time, and lacks continuous adaptability to acute physiological or environmental shifts. This paper presents a Multi-Agent Large Language Model (LLM) and Rule-Hybrid Architecture designed to structure constitutional classification and generate source-grounded lifestyle (Vihara), dietary (Ahara), and botanical (Aushadha) educational recommendations. By decoupling diagnostic sub-tasks across specialized cooperative agents and enforcing a deterministic rule-verification engine, the proposed framework separates stable baseline traits from transient symptom fluctuations while constraining unsupported generative outputs. Evaluated on a held-out synthetic benchmark cohort of 200 multi-modal profiles (derived from a 250-profile curated dataset) labeled by a consensus panel of three certified Ayurvedic physicians, the framework achieves an overall classification accuracy of 90.0%, a macro-F1 score of 0.892, and a system-to-consensus Cohen's kappa of κ=0.863(95% CI: 0.808–0.918). Ablation experiments against deterministic rule baselines and monolithic single-LLM configurations demonstrate that multi-agent task separation combined with deterministic safety gating eliminates 100.0% of predefined contraindication rule violations across benchmark and adversarial stress tests. Adhering to TRIPOD+AI reporting standards, we detail the knowledge-base provenance, system failure modes, computational overhead, and human-in-the-loop governance required for responsible deployment in integrative health informatics. items.title: A Pedagogical Framework Based on Design Dissection to Drive Innovation in Technically Complex Product Design Education
items.abstract: Designing innovative products integrated with technically complex product de- sign focused on user centric remains a significant challenges in design education. Product dissec- tion has been utilized as one of the efficient methods to interact the products to understand its working principle and to generate creative outcomes. The proposed pedagogical framework focus mainly on the functional understanding of the product being dissected. The purpose of the pro- posed work is to investigate the effectiveness of the students learning rate with respect to the product types such as mechanical, and electrical. The approach of the investigation deals with the design dissection of various products as a core teaching methods. The application of particular design thinking methods such as SCAMPER, and Morphological Matrix as blend with design dissection increase the creative outcomes. Technical realizability, ergonomic, user experience, compliance with standard and novelty are the metrics to evaluate the design outcomes. Better understanding of the various domain principles of components with functional complexities leads to innovative concepts and new product design. The findings from this investigation expose the understanding of products through the design dissection and the effectiveness in the creative design.

items.title: A Physics-Informed Surrogate Safety Gate for Agentic AI Control of SMT Reflow Soldering in Unmanned-System Electronics Manufacturing: A Simulation-Based Study
items.abstract: Surface mount technology (SMT) assembly lines running under high-mix low-volume (HMLV) conditions face a recurring parameter-optimization problem, because frequent product changeovers invalidate static control recipes and expose the nonlinear coupling between solder paste printing and reflow soldering. A large language model (LLM) can reason about that coupling. Its outputs are probabilistic and its inference latency is network-dependent, so it cannot be wired directly to process actuators. This paper takes that obstacle as its research question. The proposed multilayer Agentic AI and physics-informed digital twin (Agentic AI-DT) framework, a digital-twin architecture evaluated here as a digital model driven by a simulated closed loop, places a cloud-hosted LLM in the strategy role and an edge-deployed conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE), trained with a thermodynamic partial differential equation residual penalty, in the role of a gate that runs the same deterministic check on every strategy before it reaches the reflow oven controller. The check executes deterministically, but its verdicts inherit the surrogate's prediction error, so the safety it provides is measured here and not assumed. The study measures the gate itself: how often it fires, and how often it errs in each direction. A two-stage pipeline combining Latin Hypercube Sampling with singular value decomposition based reduced-order modelling expands 1,000 calibrated finite element simulations into 50,000 training scenarios, and 200 further independent finite element runs form the held-out test set. On those runs the physics-informed CVAE reaches a mean squared error of 1.93 ℃ 2 , 25.2% below a CVAE trained without the physics term and 14.6% below a standalone physics-informed neural network. Across 347 candidate strategies the gate vetoes 63 (18.2%). Finite element re-simulation shows that 5 of the 284 admitted candidates (1.76%, 95% CI 0.8 to 4.1%) were unsafe and that 14 of the 63 vetoed candidates (22.2%, 95% CI 13.7 to 33.9%) were safe, giving 94.5% agreement with the reference solver. Closed-loop profile tracking error is 2.09 ℃, against 3.18 ℃ for model predictive control and 4.62 ℃ for fixed-gain PID. The diagnostic layer names the injected root cause in 84.0% of 300 scripted fault trials, against 72.7% for a random forest classifier and 61.3% for a rule-based expert system. Median end-to-end latency is 419 ms, 90.7% of 2,000 cycles finish inside the 500 ms design budget, and the remaining cycles commit a re-checked last validated setpoint at the 500 ms boundary, reaching the controller within 539 ms. Every number reported here comes from a synthetic environment calibrated against three published sets of measured reflow profiles. No physical production line was instrumented, so these are simulation-fidelity measurements rather than production performance guarantees.

items.title: A proposed HTTPS Like Security Layer for AI agent actions: it asks "will this action do exactly what it was authorized to do?"
items.abstract: The internet already has strong answers for many security questions. TCP/IP delivers data. HTTPS and TLS encrypt the connection and confirm the server’s identity. OAuth grants an application access to an account. Identity systems confirm who a user or workload is. Logs and monitoring record what happened afterwards. Each of these remains essential, and each answers a question about the connection, the identity, or the record. AI agents raise a different question. An agent can now call APIs, send emails, export files, initiate payments, change databases, reconfigure cloud infrastructure, issue network commands, and control physical devices, often in milliseconds and without a human in the loop. A request can travel over a perfectly secure HTTPS connection, carry a valid OAuth token, and come from an authenticated agent, yet carry the wrong amount, the wrong destination, an expired approval, a revoked permission, a replayed request, or an instruction injected into the agent through a malicious prompt. By the time monitoring raises an alert, the payment has settled, the data has left, and the system has changed. This disclosure proposes a security layer above HTTPS that verifies each action at the moment it takes effect. Every action an AI agent proposes is held in a pending state with no external effect. A protected component, outside the agent’s control, checks that specific action against the conditions that apply: who authorized it, for what purpose, to which destination, under which policy version, within which time window, and whether permission has since been revoked. When every check passes, it issues a single-use authorization bound to that exact action and to the specific system that will carry it out. That system, whether an API gateway, payment processor, cloud control plane, network egress gateway, database, or device controller, verifies the authorization and consumes it in the same step as execution. An altered, replayed, expired, or unverified action stays blocked, and alternate routes to the same effect, such as backup systems, debug interfaces, or direct device access, pass through the same check. The layer works alongside HTTPS, OAuth, identity management, and existing access controls, and requires none of them to change. It applies to AI agents and tool calls, cloud operations, payments, telecommunications, and critical infrastructure. HTTPS secures the connection; this layer ensures each action does exactly what it was authorized to do. items.title: A Relational Framework for Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Shared Decision Making
items.abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) can support clinical decision making, but accuracy, usability, and efficiency do not establish whether patients understand options or influence the agreed plan. This study aimed to develop observable relational requirements for AI-assisted shared decision making. Methods: We conducted a qualitative framework synthesis of 21 clinical, empirical, conceptual, and governance sources identified through structured purposive sampling completed on 20 September 2026. Two-pass coding combined established shared decision-making categories with inductive analysis of AI-related relational effects. Domains were retained when supported across source types, conceptually distinct, observable at the point of care, and linked to a clinical or organizational response. Results: The synthesis identified a patient–clinician–AI interaction embedded in organizational governance and highlighted five relational concerns: apparent authority of AI output, insufficient verification and contestability, substitution of inferred for expressed preferences, uncertainty without actionable follow-up, and fragmented responsibility. These concerns informed five domains: role and influence disclosure; independent verification and contestability; direct preference elicitation; actionable uncertainty and revisability; and distributed accountability and continuity. Each domain was translated into a relational question, a clinical test, and a documentation or governance response. A complementary measurement framework distinguished technical performance from decision process, relational quality, equity, safety and continuity, and governance outcomes. Conclusions: The study’s contribution is an operational framework connecting AI-related relational concerns to observable clinical requirements and candidate evaluation measures. The proposed framework requires stakeholder and prospective clinical validation; it does not establish clinical effectiveness.

items.title: A Resource- and Power-Efficient FPGA Implementation of a Segmented Chebyshev Tanh Activation Function Using Single-Precision Floating-Point Arithmetic
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence and machine learning workloads increasingly rely on dedicated hardware accelerators, including field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), which offer parallelism and reconfigurability. The hyperbolic tangent (tanh) is widely used as a nonlinear activation function yet is costly to evaluate directly in hardware, making efficient approximation essential. This work presents an FPGA implementation of a segmented Chebyshev-polynomial-based tanh core for IEEE-754 single-precision floating-point. The input domain x∈[−6,6] is reduced to |x|∈[0,6] by exploiting tanh’s odd symmetry, and partitioned into three sub-intervals with per-interval Chebyshev degrees selected to achieve the target accuracy. Polynomial evaluation is performed via Clenshaw’s recurrence, with a single recurrence stage reused for all evaluation steps under finite-state-machine control. Implemented and verified on an Altera Cyclone V FPGA, the core uses 1176 adaptive logic modules, 317 registers, and one digital signal processing (DSP) block. It requires 28 clock cycles for inputs within the approximation domain and 3 outside it, and dissipates 6.20 mW of dynamic power at 40 MHz. The mean absolute error is 8.26×10−8 across the tested inputs and 5.74×10−8 over a denser MATLAB sweep. Against exponential-based, continued-fraction-based, and polynomial-based tanh approximations, it achieves the lowest register, DSP, memory, and dynamic power utilization.

items.title: A Review of AI-Based Job Portal Systems for Intelligent Job Matching and Recruitment
items.abstract: The growth of digital recruitment has created large volumes of job postings, candidate profiles, resumes, applications, and interaction data. Conventional job portals mainly support job publication, keyword search, filtering, application submission, and employer-side candidate management. Although these functions improve access to employment opportunities, they do not always solve the core matching problem: identifying the most relevant job for a candidate and the most suitable candidate for an employer. Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and recommender-system techniques provide opportunities to improve this process by understanding skills, experience, qualifications, job descriptions, preferences, and historical interactions. This review paper examines research on job recommender systems, e-recruitment recommendation, semantic job matching, resume screening, deep-learning-based talent recommendation, and algorithmic fairness. The literature indicates a progression from content-based and collaborative filtering toward hybrid, semantic, and deep-learning approaches. Recent studies further emphasize explainability, fairness, semantic embeddings, and large-language-model-assisted recruitment. Based on the reviewed literature, this paper proposes an AI-enabled job portal architecture combining a React Native mobile client, Spring Boot backend, MySQL database, and Python-based AI services. The proposed architecture supports role-based access for job seekers, employers, and administrators; resume processing; skill extraction; semantic candidate-job matching; personalized job recommendations; application tracking; employer notifications; and chatbot assistance. The paper identifies major research gaps involving cold-start users, limited public recruitment datasets, explainability, fairness, dynamic job preferences, and integration of multiple recruitment functions into a practical end-to-end platform. Finally, evaluation metrics and an experimental methodology are proposed for assessing recommendation quality, classification performance, response time, usability, and fairness.

items.title: A Review of Machine Learning Approaches to Eye Disease Detection: Current Trends, Challenges and Future Directions
items.abstract: Background/Objectives: Vision impairment and blindness remain a major global health challenge, with glaucoma, diabetic retinopathy, age-related macular degeneration, cataract, corneal disease, and retinopathy of prematurity representing important causes of preventable or treatable vision loss when detected early. This clinical need has accelerated research on machine learning approaches for automatic detection of eye diseases, grading, and segmentation. However, existing reviews often focus on a single disease or method. They also give limited attention to their suitability and applicability for reliable clinical deployments. This review synthesizes traditional machine learning, deep learning, vision transformers, ensemble and hybrid models, segmentation methods, and explainable AI approaches for eye disease detection. It further examines task formulation, dataset characteristics, evaluation practices, and deployment constraints, with emphasis on clinical readiness rather than benchmark performance alone. Methods: A structured narrative review was conducted using recently published articles from reputable databases and repositories, including IEEE Xplore, PubMed/MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus and arXiv. The review critically analyzes the progression from traditional machine learning to advanced models, including deep learning, vision transformers, ensemble models and explainable artificial intelligence. Studies were critically analyzed according to task formulations, dataset characteristics, segmentation approaches, evaluation metrics, explainability, and deployment constraints. Results: The synthesis shows that class imbalance, limited demographic and geographic diversity in available datasets, weak external validation, and scarce prospective evidence continue to separate benchmark performance from clinical readiness. Explainability is also often evaluated through visual plausibility rather than validated faithfulness. Currently, data-driven diabetic retinopathy screening is closest to clinical readiness, particularly for distinguishing referable from non-referable cases, whereas multi-label detection, rare disease detection, and cross-device deployment remain at the research stage. Conclusions: Progress towards clinical adoption requires stronger alignment between experimental evaluation and real-world deployment. This includes external validation and the development of equitable, interpretable, and resource-aware systems.

items.title: A Review of Machine Learning Techniques for Analog-To-Digital Converter Design Automation
items.abstract: ADCs play an important role in converting information from the analog world to the digital one; with modern applications requiring higher resolutions, speed, and power efficiency, it has become very difficult to design them. Traditionally, the design of an ADC follows an iterative design process that includes stages like specification, behavioral modeling, transistor sizing, schematic simulation, layout, and post-layout verification, which is laborious and requires much designer expertise due to the consideration of process-voltage-temperature variations and yield. In this work, we perform a review of the latest advancements in the use of machine learning (ML) to tackle the challenges of ADC design in recent years, with systematic search from 2015 to 2026 in IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and arXiv. Rather than organizing the literature on different ML algorithms, this paper categorizes ML approaches such as regression, tree-based models, SVM, ANN, CNN, GNN, reinforcement learning, evolutionary algorithms, and Bayesian optimization in ADC design stages such as behavioral modeling, transistor sizing, calibration of comparators and capacitor arrays, calibration of ADC, layout optimization, prediction of PVT/yield variations, and design space exploration. Comparative analysis includes the benefits provided by each technique such as speed and accuracy improvements, as well as their main drawbacks. Open challenges are then presented, including lack of data, poor generalization performance, low explainability, and the largely unexplored topic of co-optimization across multiple stages. Finally, future trends in the field are presented in terms of new directions such as generative AI, GNN-based layout optimization, physics-informed learning, digital twins, and human-AI collaborative design, as well as risks and potential problems such as manufacturability and IP in generative approaches

items.title: A Scoping Review of Sentiment Analysis for Customer Satisfaction in Digital Banking: Mapping the Research Gap Toward Multimodal Integration
items.abstract: Sentiment analysis has become increasingly important for interpreting customer-generated content across social media and digital technologies. However, research on digital banking continues to rely predominantly on textonly data, with limited attention to multimodal integration. This scoping review mapped the literature on sentiment analysis for customer satisfaction in digital banking, identified research gaps, and outlined future directions. The review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and searched six databases—ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, Wiley Online Library, ACM Digital Library, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar—for English-language studies published from 2015 to 2026; the final search was conducted on May 10, 2026. Of 1,631 records identified, 35 studies met the inclusion criteria. Text only data were used in 31 studies (88.6%), multi-source text was used in one study (2.9%), text combined with survey data in two studies (5.7%), and numerical time-series data in one study (2.9%); no included study integrated text, audio, and video within a single sentiment analysis framework. The literature was geographically concentrated and relied mainly on traditional machine-learning and hybrid approaches, whereas transformer/LLM based methods, explainable AI, and real-time approaches remained limited. The absence of banking-specific multimodal datasets is a key barrier to progress. Future research should prioritize privacy-preserving multimodal datasets, multilingual and culturally diverse models, explainable AI, and real-time deployment to support more reliable assessment of customer experience in digital banking.

items.title: A Scoping Review on Intelligent Computing upon Silicon Photonics and Optical Network on Chips
items.abstract: The continuous expansion of data-intensive applications, including deep learning, autonomous control, and real-time analytics, has pushed conventional electronic computing toward its limits in performance and energy efficiency. Combining silicon photonics with Optical Network on Chip (ONoC) provides a pathway toward high-bandwidth and low-latency communication with reduced power consumption, positioning these technologies as promising enablers for next-generation intelligent systems. This work systematically reviews current efforts to integrate silicon photonics and ONoC architectures with Artificial Intelligence (AI) models such as Machine Learning (ML), Deep Neural Network (DNN), and Large Language Model (LLM), highlighting recent progress, application areas, and open research challenges. A structured literature review was carried out across two focus areas, each searched and screened as a separate stream: (1) Optical Neural Network (ONN) developed for AI inference and training, and (2) ML-based optimization techniques applied to ONoC design. Peer-reviewed studies, and preprints under an explicitly stated rule, were examined with attention to device-level innovations, architectural co-design, acceleration of AI workloads, and photonic-aware system optimization. Recent studies report advances in photonic devices such as modulators, detectors, and microring resonators, along with hybrid photonic–electronic architectures and AI-optimized routing frameworks. ONN implementations demonstrate high-speed, low-energy computation, while ML-assisted methods have improved ONoC performance in wavelength allocation, fault tolerance, and security. Despite rapid progress, several technical challenges remain, including fabrication tolerances, thermal sensitivity, and the limited maturity of nonlinear photonic components. Current demonstrations are mainly at the prototype level, with few large-scale deployments, and because most studies are simulation-based, their reported performance figures should be regarded as upper bounds that still require verification on fabricated hardware. The convergence of silicon photonics, ONoCs, and AI computing represents a shift from purely electronic processing toward hybrid photonic–electronic platforms capable of supporting massive workloads efficiently. Future research should emphasize scalable fabrication processes, integrated photonic–electronic co-design, robust thermal management, and standardized frameworks to accelerate the adoption of these technologies in AI accelerators, data centers, and edge devices.

items.title: A Step-Level Reliability Gateway for Agentic Clinical Decision Support: Architecture and Edge Deployment
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents now retrieve patient records, call risk models and draft alerts in clinical workflows, yet their safety checks usually inspect only the final output. We present a reliability gateway that checks each action a clinical agent proposes, before it runs, and allows it, defers it to a clinician or blocks it. The decision fuses five run-time signals: calibration among similar patients, subgroup calibration gaps, group-conditional conformal sets, drift state and alert timing, plus a check that alerts quote tool outputs correctly. We generated agent trajectories with a local 7-billion-parameter model on emergency department (MIMIC-IV-ED) and intensive care (eICU-CRD) cohorts, injected six fault types at known steps, froze thresholds on a tuning split and replayed held-out trajectories. In the emergency setting, the gateway stopped 62% of faulty trajectories at the fault step, against 31% for an output-only check, with false intervention on 7.0% of clean trajectories. On held-out intensive care hospitals, its drift signal deferred every request. On a Raspberry Pi 5 the 99th-percentile latency per gated action was 25.8 ms, almost all of it from the nearest-neighbour signal, which added no measurable detection in the emergency setting. Step-level gating is feasible on embedded hardware; which signals are worth their cost depends on the deployment.

items.title: A Study on AI-Based Customer Relationship Management in Modern Commerce
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing how firms interpret customer records, support service employees and communicate across commercial channels. Its value depends on the quality of the relationship it helps maintain. This paper examines AI-based customer relationship management through a critical narrative review and descriptive analysis of published evidence. Nine journal articles are considered alongside official enterprise statistics and an AI risk framework. The review distinguishes ordinary CRM adoption from the deployment of AI within CRM. It also separates operational productivity from customer trust and durable commercial value. Two charts reproduce attributed Eurostat observations, while an original conceptual diagram connects data readiness, bounded assistance, human decisions and relationship outcomes. The synthesis suggests that useful deployment requires clear task boundaries, reliable knowledge sources, accessible correction and evaluation beyond response speed. A proposed implementation roadmap and research propositions identify ways to examine these conditions in future field studies. No primary survey, customer experiment or statistical hypothesis test is reported. The paper contributes a practical basis for studying AI-assisted relationships without treating software ownership, automation volume or conversational fluency as proof of customer benefit..

items.title: A Survey of Agentic Robotics: Toward Continual Self-Improvement
items.abstract: Foundation models (FMs), particularly large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs), are increasingly used as the decision-making core of AI agents and are now being extended from digital environments to robotic systems. In classical robotics, engineers decompose tasks, specify objectives, write control code, and repair failures before deployment; in agentic robotics, an FM makes some of these decisions at run time or during improvement. Bringing this paradigm into the physical world introduces additional challenges: FM-mediated decisions must be grounded in executable robot behavior, respect physical constraints, and close the loop through real-world feedback. We survey this emerging paradigm and organize existing systems by three loci of FM-mediated agency: task orchestration, motion/action generation, and improvement. Coding rules for each locus make the definition operational, including a test of which improvement decisions the FM makes that separates fixed-procedure from agent-directed improvement. We apply these rules to the systems retrieved by a systematic search, examine verification and feedback-closure mechanisms, and compare what self-improving systems have demonstrated. Finally, we discuss continual self-improvement as a central emerging frontier and the challenges toward reliable autonomous improvement through physical interaction.

items.title: A System Dynamics Approach to AI Risk Governance and Organizational Resilience in SMEs: Modeling the Trade-off Between Innovation and Compliance
items.abstract: This paper is building a system dynamics model to investigate how the small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) can regulate artificial intelligence (AI) risk without reducing the innovation value that can be justified when implementing AI. The work contends that the relationship between innovation and compliance is not a linear kind of trade-off, but a dynamical regulatory system with feedback mechanisms whereby experimentation, deployment levels, risk exposure, governance mechanisms, learning routines, and resilience resources interact with one another through time. The paper incorporates the constructs of SMEs into a stock-flow simulation based on the dynamic capabilities theory, organizational resilience research, technology-organization-environment logic, AI risk management standards, and system dynamics. Findings indicate that innovation-first strategy generates rapid initial ability development and generates shadow AI, risks that were not fully resolved, more recovery time, and shorter resilience. Compliance first approach minimizes risk exposure at the cost of experimentation and introduces approval lag. Balanced adaptive governance is the strongest in the long-term outcome where tiered controls, learning loops, human oversight, and reusable compliance routines minimize risk without impacting the innovation throughput. The article adds a dynamic conceptualization of AI risk governance among SMEs and the leverage points to use by managers and policymakers aiming at responsible adoption of AI given the limited resources.

items.title: Accuracy and Safety of Three Large Language Models Answering Turkish Questions on Adult Immunization
items.abstract: Vaccine misinformation contributes to falling immunization coverage, and people increasingly bring vaccine questions to chatbots. We evaluated three large language models on 72 Turkish questions on adult immunization, in two arms: 40 patient-focused questions and 32 mapped to CDC/ACIP, WHO or Turkish Ministry of Health recommendations. The 216 responses were blind-coded and scored independently by two blinded specialists against a guideline-anchored answer key. Binary accuracy was 95.1% for Claude Opus 4.8, 93.8% for Gemini-3.1-Pro, and 86.1% for GPT-5.5. Patient-facing questions, including the classic vaccine myths, were answered well (93.8–96.2%), but accuracy on technical guideline content fell to 76.6% for GPT-5.5, which was also the most readable model and referred the reader to a clinician in only 53.1% of guideline-arm responses. Responses were more often incomplete than wrong.

items.title: Adaptive Digital Consciousness: An Evolutionary Framework for Human Identity Preservation Using Large Language Models
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) have greatly changed the interaction between man and machines through natural-language reasoning, content generation, personalization, and interaction via agents. However, traditional LLM applications do not provide a unified mechanism for maintaining a long-term, structured, and identity-consistent representation of a person during long-time interaction. As shown in the recent studies of generative agents, long-term LLM memory, agentic memory, lifelong learning, and AI self-identity, these processes present essential capabilities that have been studied as separate components. This paper presents the Adaptive Digital Consciousness (ADC) framework as the theoretical architecture for computational representation of core features of human identity. The ADC framework proposes a system of structured representation of Digital DNA for personal knowledge, experience, preferences, values, and behaviors and connects it to multilayer memory, semantic embeddings, vector retrieval, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), LLM reasoning, adaptive learning, and autonomous agents. The framework also proposes the notion of identity constraints and the system of updating memory, consolidating it, handling conflicts, forgetting, maintaining privacy, consent, and security, as well as monitoring the origin of digital information. The goal of the study is not to replicate biological or subjective consciousness The research motivation, previous works, the system suggested, as well as memory and adaptation techniques, evaluation techniques, ethics and applications of the findings, drawbacks of the research and future research directions on this subject.

items.title: Addressing Cyberbullying in Vietnam Through Generative Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Cyberbullying is not only a growing concern for society as a whole, but especially for the education sector, as it disproportionately affects the youngest cohorts, undermining learning and psychological well-being. At the same time, the increasing accessibility of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), has begun to reshape how people communicate online. Against this background, this chapter examines cyberbullying in Vietnam through the lens of GenAI, highlighting both the negative and positive dimensions of this technological shift. Using an integrative review that combines international and local scholarship, the chapter summarizes the scope (including common types) and the psychosocial consequences of cyberbullying in Vietnam. The review draws on peer-reviewed studies and local reports, organizing the findings into thematic domains to form a pragmatic analytic framework for practice and policy. The chapter then considers how GenAI capabilities – automated content generation, personalization, and deepfake technologies – may increase the speed, reach, and ambiguity of harassment, making harmful behaviors harder to identify and respond to. Conversely, it discusses the potential of AI-enabled tools for detection, moderation, risk assessment, and early warning to strengthen community- and school-based prevention systems that can be integrated with GenAI. The chapter also addresses fundamental technical and governance issues, including algorithmic bias, transparency and explainability, privacy and data protection, and safeguards for child rights in digital contexts. Overall, it argues that GenAI-based responses are likely to be effective only when integrated with Vietnamese language use, culturally specific communication norms, and existing institutional capacities. By situating Vietnam within global conversations on cyberbullying and GenAI, the chapter offers contextually appropriate recommendations to support responsible, ethical, and protective uses of GenAI for safer online spaces.

items.title: Advanced Backend Technologies using MongoDB: A Scalable NoSQL Database for Modern Web, Cloud, and AI Applications
items.abstract: Modern web applications require databases that provide high performance, flexibility, and scalability to manage large volumes of structured and unstructured data. Traditional relational databases often face challenges in handling rapidly changing application requirements. MongoDB, a leading NoSQL document-oriented database, addresses these challenges through its flexible schema, distributed architecture, and cloud-native capabilities. This paper presents a study of MongoDB and its role in advanced backend technologies. It discusses MongoDB's document model, replication, sharding, indexing, and aggregation framework along with its integration with modern backend frameworks such as Node.js, Express.js, FastAPI, and Spring Boot. The paper also explores MongoDB Atlas for cloud deployment and its applications in microservices, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Internet of Things (IoT), and Big Data. A comparison with traditional SQL databases is provided to evaluate performance, scalability, and flexibility. The study concludes that MongoDB is an efficient and future-ready database solution for building secure, scalable, and high-performance backend applications.

items.title: Advanced Ventilation Systems in Interior Spaces: Improving Indoor Air Quality and Human Comfort
items.abstract: Indoor environments have become a critical area of research due to the increasing amount of time people spend inside buildings and the growing recognition of the relationship between indoor environmental quality and human health. Modern buildings are increasingly designed with improved insulation and airtight construction to enhance energy efficiency; however, these strategies can unintentionally reduce natural air exchange and contribute to the accumulation of indoor pollutants. Poor indoor air quality (IAQ), caused by elevated carbon dioxide (CO₂), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10), biological contaminants, and excessive humidity, can negatively affect occupant health, comfort, cognitive performance, and productivity. Advanced ventilation systems have emerged as an essential solution for maintaining healthy indoor environments while achieving energy efficiency goals. Unlike conventional ventilation approaches that provide fixed airflow rates, advanced systems incorporate adaptive technologies such as demand-controlled ventilation, heat and energy recovery ventilation, displacement ventilation, personalized ventilation, and intelligent ventilation systems supported by Internet of Things (IoT) sensors and artificial intelligence (AI). These systems continuously monitor indoor conditions and adjust ventilation performance according to occupancy levels, pollutant concentrations, and environmental parameters. This review paper examines the development, operational principles, and applications of advanced ventilation technologies in interior spaces. It explores their role in improving indoor air quality, enhancing thermal comfort, reducing energy consumption, and supporting sustainable interior design practices. The paper also discusses the integration of smart monitoring systems, occupant-centered ventilation strategies, and future directions toward adaptive and self-learning building environments. Through a comprehensive analysis of existing research, this review highlights the importance of advanced ventilation systems as a fundamental component of healthy, efficient, and human-centered interior spaces.

items.title: Advancing neurosurgical practice with augmented reality: a single-center real-world case series with illustrated technical notes
items.abstract: OBJECTIVE The aim of this study was to evaluate the real-world application and clinical value of a head-mounted augmented reality (AR) navigation platform across a wide range of neurosurgical pathologies and procedures. METHODS In this real-world retrospective case series, the authors assessed 105 neurosurgical procedures performed by 8 neurosurgeons at a single center from January 2024 to March 2026. A head-mounted AR navigation platform (SurgicalAR, Cranial Navigation, and Spine Navigation; Medivis) was used in all procedures. Video records were available for all cases. Clinical and pathological data, surgical approaches, types of reference frames, and registration methods were systematically collected. The workflow for each surgical approach was characterized in detail. RESULTS This analysis included 105 cases (60 female, mean age 53.5). Cranial surgeries (n = 92, 87.6%) were most common, predominantly for tumors (n = 69, 65.7%), with meningioma (22.9%) and glioblastoma (19.0%) as the leading pathologies. Custom reference frames (n = 57) and surface registration (n = 93) were the most frequently used techniques in cranial navigation. In cranial tumor surgery, gross-total resection was achieved in 62 of 69 cases, supported by multimodal AR planning. In spine surgery, all 34 pedicle screws placed with the Spine Navigation system achieved a Gertzbein-Robbins grade of A. AR was also successfully applied to cerebrovascular, puncture-based, and functional surgery. CONCLUSIONS Head-mounted AR navigation was feasible across diverse procedures, but its value depended on case selection, registration reliability, and workflow. It was most useful for multimodal tumor planning, pedicle screw placement, and percutaneous interventions; conventional navigation or direct anatomical guidance remained necessary when AR accuracy or ergonomics were inadequate. These findings support AR as a significant advancement in future neurosurgical practice.

items.title: Advancing value creation in B2B market research – a human–AI collaboration framework for large language model
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how prompt design influences the quality of large language model (LLM)-generated business-to-business (B2B) market research outputs. It also proposes a switch-point governance mechanism for converting LLM-generated drafts into decision-ready market intelligence artefacts. Design/methodology/approach The study uses an exploratory pilot evaluation of three market-facing LLM-based tools: ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity AI. The tools are compared across three benchmark B2B market research tasks and three prompt types: basic, context-augmented and role-specific. In total, 81 outputs were generated. A role-specific benchmark subset of 27 outputs was then assessed using automated metrics and blinded human ratings. The automated metrics included relevance through cosine similarity, reference overlap through ROUGE-F1, cross-run semantic stability, latency, token length and readability through Flesch Reading Ease. Human evaluators rated the outputs on relevance, completeness, factuality, instruction-following and insightfulness. One-way ANOVA and non-parametric checks are reported as exploratory task-level tests, not as confirmatory evidence of model superiority. Findings Role-specific prompts produced the strongest descriptive scores in this pilot setting. Within the benchmark subset, Gemini showed the strongest observed profile, with higher average relevance, reference overlap and semantic stability, along with lower latency. ChatGPT produced relevant outputs but tended to generate longer and less readable drafts. Perplexity generated concise and readable summaries, but its outputs were less aligned with the reference brief and decision-facing requirements. Human ratings followed a similar descriptive pattern. Cross-run semantic stability showed directional alignment with higher decision-readiness ratings, offering preliminary support for P1. The proposed switch-point matrix illustrates P2 by mapping automated confidence signals and human judgement to four escalation actions: accept, judge, review/redo and rewrite. Research limitations/implications The study is an exploratory pilot case. The task set is small, and the task-level ANOVA is based on only three observations per tool. The findings may also vary across domains, model versions, prompt libraries and organisational contexts. Future research should expand the task bank, include more B2B sectors, use larger rater pools, compare additional model versions and test the switch-point thresholds in live market intelligence workflows. Practical implications The study provides a replicable workflow for B2B market intelligence teams. It shows how teams can standardise prompt design, screen LLM-generated outputs, combine automated checks with human evaluation and allocate decision rights through transparent escalation rules. Social implications The framework supports accountable use of LLM-based market research by reducing the risk that persuasive but weakly grounded claims enter managerial decision-making. It also highlights the need for human oversight; evidence checks and traceable governance in AI-supported knowledge work. Originality/value The study extends service-dominant logic to LLM-mediated B2B market research by treating LLM outputs as candidate value propositions rather than finished knowledge products. Its main contribution is the operationalisation of decision-rights governance through cross-run semantic stability and switch-point logic.

items.title: Aesthetics in form and Function: Ergonomic Analysis of Juice Glassware
items.abstract: Glassware serves both functional and experiential roles in juice service, where design influences usability, visual appeal, and perceived capacity. This study examines the ergonomic and aesthetic attributes of commonly used glassware and their effects on volumetric efficiency and user experience. Glass samples collected from juice shops across the Vellore district, Tamil Nadu, were analysed through empirical observation. Ergonomic parameters included grip comfort, stability, dimensional balance, and weight distribution, while aesthetic qualities such as form, clarity, texture, and design language were evaluated through structured user surveys. Findings indicate that Collins glasses are the predominant choice for fresh juice, with mason jars and standard bottles also preferred, whereas sling and pint glasses are seldom selected. Overall, 84% of users favoured ergonomically optimised designs. The study concludes that combining ergonomic efficiency with aesthetic coherence enhances functionality, presentation, and consumer satisfaction.

items.title: AI adoption statistics 2026: How far along is your industry?
items.abstract: AI adoption is moving quickly, but not every company or industry is progressing at the same pace. Some organizations have already integrated AI into daily operations, while others are still experimenting with early use cases. Looking at AI adoption statistics can help business leaders understand where the market stands and whether their own company is ahead, catching up, or still at the beginning of the adoption journey. What AI adoption statistics reveal AI adoption data provides more than a snapshot of how many companies are using artificial intelligence. It can also show how businesses move from experimentation to practical implementation and where AI is becoming part of everyday operations. For companies planning their next steps, AI adoption statistics can provide useful context. They help decision makers compare their progress with broader market activity and understand whether investment in AI is accelerating across their sector. AI adoption by industry Different sectors face different challenges when adopting AI. AI adoption by industry can vary depending on available data, regulatory requirements, technical maturity, business processes, and the types of problems companies are trying to solve. Healthcare, finance, retail, manufacturing, and professional services may all approach AI differently. Some industries can introduce automation and analytics quickly, while others need more preparation before AI can be integrated into critical workflows. Understanding these differences helps companies compare themselves with organizations operating in similar environments rather than treating AI adoption as a single market-wide trend. Enterprise AI adoption For large organizations, AI adoption often becomes more complicated once companies move beyond individual pilots. Enterprise AI adoption statistics can show how businesses are scaling AI across departments, where investments are being made, and which obstacles continue to slow broader implementation. Common challenges may include data readiness, internal skills, coordination between teams, and the ability to connect AI initiatives with clear business goals. Looking at enterprise adoption patterns can help decision makers understand what other organizations are prioritizing and where implementation often becomes difficult. AI adoption trends in 2026 Current AI adoption trends suggest that companies are increasingly focused on practical results rather than experimentation alone. Businesses are looking at how AI can improve operations, customer experience, analytics, and automation while delivering measurable value. However, adoption still depends heavily on factors such as industry maturity, data quality, internal expertise, and leadership support. Companies that understand these constraints can set more realistic expectations and prioritize AI initiatives that are more likely to succeed. Final thoughts AI adoption in 2026 is not happening at the same speed everywhere. Some businesses are already scaling AI across operations, while others are still building the foundations needed for successful implementation. By examining AI adoption statistics, AI adoption by industry, enterprise AI adoption statistics, and broader AI adoption trends, companies can better understand their position in the market and make more informed decisions about where to focus their next AI investments.

items.title: AI and Machine Learning for API Security
items.abstract: This research paper explores the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) in enhancing Application Programming Interface (API) security. It focuses on real-time API monitoring, anomaly detection, behavioral analysis, threat identification, risk classification, and automated security responses. The study reviews six existing research works and proposes an AI-driven security framework that classifies incoming API requests into three categories: safe, suspicious, and malicious. Based on the identified risk level, the proposed system aims to allow legitimate requests, verify suspicious activities, and block potentially harmful requests while maintaining security logs for further analysis. The paper also highlights key challenges, including false alarms, data quality, computational requirements, and adapting to evolving cyber threats. It presents a conceptual framework and future evaluation approach to support the development of more intelligent, adaptive, and reliable API security systems.

items.title: AI and the Right to Privacy: A Comparative Study of India and the European Union
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence has turned privacy from a question of disclosure alone into one of continuous data collection, inference, prediction and consequential decision-making. This Article asks whether Indian law offers protection against such forms of data-intensive power that is as layered as that of the European Union. It adopts a doctrinal and comparative approach, analysing constitutional rights, data protection laws, artificial intelligence legislation, key case law, institutional documents and enforcement data. India has a solid constitutional framework for dignity, autonomy and proportionality, but its statutory framework is less specific on solely automated decisions, explanations, meaningful human intervention, biometric surveillance and model training. This gap is widened by the phased commencement of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, under which a number of substantive obligations had yet to come into force as of September 2026. The European Union, by comparison, combines the Charter of Fundamental Rights, the General Data Protection Regulation and the Artificial Intelligence Act, producing more detailed rules on lawful processing, sensitive data, automated decisions, risk management and transparency. The European model is nonetheless fragmented and highly technical, especially on model training, data inferred by models, and the blurred boundary between data protection law and the new artificial intelligence law. The comparison points to a calibrated Indian reform agenda built on contestability, high-risk impact assessment, biometric safeguards, training-data accountability and independent technical oversight, rather than wholesale transplantation of the European Union regime.

items.title: AI Anxiety, Familiarity and Privacy Concerns: The Mediating Role of AI Literacy and the Moderating Role of Technophobia
items.abstract: This study examines how AI anxiety and familiarity relate to privacy concerns through AI literacy, and whether technophobia moderates the literacy–privacy relationship. Using survey data from 3,000 generative AI users in China and partial least squares structural equation modeling, we find that both familiarity and, contrary to expectations, anxiety are positively associated with AI literacy. AI literacy, in turn, is associated with greater privacy concerns and mediates both relationships, suggesting that increased knowledge may heighten awareness of data risks. Technophobia weakens the positive association between AI literacy and privacy concerns, although more technophobic users report higher overall concern. Exploratory age-group analyses suggest that the positive anxiety–literacy association is especially apparent among users in their 40s. These findings reveal a privacy awareness paradox and highlight the value of AI education that combines technical understanding, privacy awareness, and attention to users’ emotional responses.

items.title: AI Enhanced Anomaly Detection of System Logs in Cybersecurity
items.abstract: System logs contain valuable information about authentication attempts, application events, operating system activities, and potential cybersecurity threats. However, manually analysing large volumes of log data is time-consuming and may delay the detection of suspicious activities. This paper presents an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enhanced system for detecting anomalous patterns in system logs using machine learning techniques. The proposed workflow includes log collection, preprocessing, time-window aggregation, feature extraction, anomaly scoring, threshold-based classification, and security alert generation. Isolation Forest is used as the primary unsupervised anomaly detection algorithm and is compared with Local Outlier Factor (LOF), One-Class Support Vector Machine (SVM), Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) autoencoder. The evaluation uses a simulated dataset containing 30,000 one-hour activity windows, including 1,050 injected anomaly windows. The reported results show that Isolation Forest achieves a precision of 0.594, recall of 0.553, F1-score of 0.573, ROC-AUC of 0.962, and average precision of 0.613. Although Isolation Forest provides a lightweight detection approach, the comparison indicates that other methods achieve higher F1-scores under the reported experimental conditions. The findings highlight the importance of threshold selection, class imbalance, and multiple evaluation metrics in anomaly detection. The proposed workflow provides a foundation for cybersecurity monitoring and suspicious-activity prioritisation. Further validation using real-world enterprise logs is required to establish its effectiveness in practical deployment.

items.title: AI Facilitation of Online Disagreement
items.abstract: AI has considerable potential to facilitate online discussions and reduce conflict, but designers of such systems face the risk of algorithmic aversion. Past studies have found that people judge identical messages less favorably when they believe they were written by AI. However, as AI becomes more integrated into everyday life and people gain experience with AI facilitators, this aversion may diminish. It also remains unclear how much the content of a facilitator's message matters relative to its human or AI label, and whether the facilitation strategies people prefer actually improve the conversation. Finally, because most people observe rather than participate in online discussions, it is important to understand whether AI facilitators are perceived differently by observers and participants. To address these questions, we conducted two complementary studies examining perceptions of different facilitation strategies and their effects on actual conversations. In a vignette experiment (N = 388), we crossed the facilitator's label (AI or human) with ten facilitation strategies. In a live conversation experiment, an LLM used five of these strategies to facilitate 20-minute text chats between 188 pairs of people who disagreed on political and non-political topics. Participants preferred the kind of facilitator they had experienced. After seeing an AI facilitator, 30% wanted one in future discussions, against 7% after seeing a human facilitator. The AI label lowered ratings of the facilitator's warmth and competence, but the strategy mattered far more, explaining 11% of the variance in ratings against less than 1% explained by the label. Participants preferred facilitators that showed understanding over facilitators that reminded them of community norms. However, the strategies people preferred did not reliably change the conversations. Observers and participants in live conversations ranked the strategies similarly. In summary, the AI vs. human label matters far less than what the facilitator actually says. A well-designed process can improve user perceptions more than enough to offset algorithmic aversion.

items.title: AI in Indian Healthcare: Promise, Pitfalls, and the Path Forward
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping healthcare in India through diagnostic imaging, predictive analytics, robotic surgery, patient monitoring, and hospital workflow automation. These innovations promise improved diagnostic accuracy, operational efficiency, and expanded access to care, particularly in resource-limited settings. Yet, accelerated adoption raises critical challenges, including inadequate regulation, weak data governance, cybersecurity risks, patient privacy concerns, and algorithmic bias, which may undermine trust and equitable care delivery. This study employed a mixed-methods design to explore perceptions of 69 purposively sampled healthcare professionals across India. A structured questionnaire assessed familiarity with AI, perceived benefits, skill-related challenges, ethical concerns, and regulatory awareness. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, while qualitative responses underwent Braun and Clarke's thematic analysis. Extracted themes were further subjected to Pareto analysis and a policy priority matrix to identify the most pressing issues. Findings show that 75.3% of participants were familiar with AI, with many recognizing its role in improving work quality (68.1%), efficiency (68.1%), and supporting clinical judgment (65.2%). However, 59% feared reduced cognitive engagement. Most (86.9%) emphasized the urgent need for new skill sets. Thematic analysis identified key concerns included limited regulatory awareness (n39), training and continuous learning needs (n25), data privacy and security (n15), patient care benefits (n13), risks of breaches and unauthorized access (n12) and specific guideline or bills(n12). The study highlights the need for comprehensive training, robust ethical and regulatory frameworks, and strong data governance to balance AI's benefits with its risks in Indian healthcare.

items.title: AI in Long-Term Care: A Closed-Loop Sociotechnical Reliability Framework
items.abstract: AI is increasingly used in long-term care (LTC), yet reliability is often judged at the level of individual models or devices. This is insufficient in LTC, where residents vary in capacity, autonomy, and preferences. Their ability to question AI outputs may fluctuate, and care delivery depends on distributed roles and finite operational capacity. We define sociotechnical reliability as the capacity of an AI-enabled care system to consistently translate resident-relevant information into appropriate and timely care actions under real-world LTC conditions, with failures that are detectable and correctable across the care pathway. In this Viewpoint, we draw on professional experience overseeing AI initiatives across LTC and hospital settings, examined in relation to a purposively mapped interdisciplinary literature, to inform the development of a reliability framework. Our aim is to reframe AI reliability in LTC as an end-to-end care system property and to provide a framework for identifying where reliability is gained, lost, and evaluated. We propose 5 reliability functions: sensing, inference, verification and contextualization, response and escalation, and learning and adaptation, with governance and accountability operating across all 5 functions. The framework highlights recurrent failures, including incomplete sensing, nonportable inference, overreliance on or dismissal of AI outputs during verification, unclear ownership or delayed response, and repeated failures without correction. The framework also makes reliability empirically examinable through questions about where the pathway fails, who has the authority to verify and act, whether response demands are sustainable within available capacity, and whether failures become visible to governance and inform learning and adaptation. Our central viewpoint is that AI in LTC should be judged not by model performance alone but by whether the surrounding care system can reliably translate AI-generated information into care.
